sources.name: Thames Water water and wastewater capacity
sources.fact: Pre-planning enquiries determine whether water/wastewater network capacity exists and what action/timing is needed if it does not

sources.name: Planning guidance water supply wastewater quality
sources.fact: Planning should align growth with necessary water/wastewater infrastructure; occupancy can be phased until required works are complete

sources.name: Water resources planning guideline 2026
sources.fact: WRMPs forecast supply and demand over at least 25 years and must consider growth and uncertainty

sources.name: Water resources planning guideline collection
sources.fact: Guideline updated 16 June 2026 and governs statutory long-term water resources planning

sources.name: National Policy Statement water resources 2025
sources.fact: Current NPS provides policy for nationally significant water resource infrastructure

sources.name: National Framework regional planning expectations
sources.fact: 2026 framework links long-term water planning to growth, resilience and environmental protection

sources.name: Drainage and Wastewater Management Plan guidance
sources.fact: Sewerage undertakers have statutory duties to prepare and maintain DWMPs

sources.name: Ofwat water resource planning
sources.fact: WRMPs and regional plans address population growth, climate change and long-term supply-demand balance

sources.name: Ofwat major water infrastructure programme
sources.fact: March 2026 programme covers major long-term infrastructure projects; strategic programme status is not local network capacity

sources.name: London Plan sustainable infrastructure
sources.fact: London policy stresses timely water infrastructure and water resilience ahead of need

sources.name: London Infrastructure Framework
sources.fact: 2026 framework identifies water supply among growth-critical infrastructure systems

sources.name: LBBD Inclusive Growth infrastructure
sources.fact: LBBD IDP assesses current provision and future infrastructure needs supporting Local Plan growth

examples: Thames Water pre-planning response is needed for scheme-specific network capacity; borough growth policy is insufficient
WRMP surplus/deficit is resource-zone evidence, not a parcel connection confirmation
Wastewater capacity and potable-water capacity are separate constraints
Strategic reservoir or regional water project does not prove local sewer capacity
DWMP planning does not prove a specific development can connect without reinforcement
SuDS/flood mitigation does not substitute for foul sewer capacity evidence
Infrastructure may need phasing before occupation where water/wastewater works are required
No water or wastewater capacity score is assigned without a site-specific utility response
